report: Reviewed the complete current claim, one ordinary implementation association and both ordinary tests. Independently verified exact byte equality of validate.rs, language.rs and value_types.rs with the supplied historical snapshots; the prior rationale remains supported by current evidence, not merely its approval. The claim requires exact declared arity for every named application, including opaque types, builtins, zero-argument parameters and nested applications. build_model records declaration parameter counts (classes zero); Model::resolve_type obtains local/qualified declared or builtin arity, treats scoped parameters as zero, rejects any unequal count, and recursively resolves generic arguments and tuple elements. check_values and class field/method checks invoke this resolver. The complete tests provide complementary evidence: checks_arity_scope_and_duplicate_members_in_value_types explicitly requires diagnostics for missing Binder arguments, applying T to Value, and excess Option arguments; arity_checks_reach_nested_named_types checks exactly one arity diagnostic separately for missing Vec arguments, excess Option arguments, bool application, Vec<Option>, and tuple-nested Vec<Option>. These cover declared, builtin and parameter categories, under/overapplication and recursive traversal. Captured both test setup helpers through review read: they parse real crate fixtures and call validate, with assertions visible in the annotated bodies. No TODO/N/A entries or deferred prerequisites exist. This is source assessment and exact baseline comparison; I ran review start/read and this recording workflow, not behavioral tests or a workspace build. The coordinator separately reports 321 functional tests and cargo build passing; those are not executions by this reviewer. No source changes or requested edits.
